entries.statement: Audit events capture actor, action, resource, tenant, result, request, trace, metadata hash, and time
Ordinary application roles cannot update or delete audit events
Audit search and export support permissioned filters and integrity evidence
Workspace admins can configure retention by data class
Users and tenants can export their data in documented formats
User deletion and tenant deletion are durable jobs with legal-hold and completion evidence
Data deletion propagates to caches, indexes, object storage, providers, and backups according to policy
Admins can configure region, model processing policy, telemetry policy, and connector allowlist
Support access is time-limited, reason-bound, approval-aware, and audited
Security center displays sessions, SSO, SCIM, domains, API credentials, webhooks, and recent risk events
Agents have stable definitions and immutable versions
Agent versions include instructions, input/output schemas, model policy, retrieval policy, tools, budgets, and guardrails
Model policies map roles to provider/model versions, fallback, residency, latency, and cost limits
Prompt and model changes are independently versioned and attributable
The model gateway normalizes requests, streaming, usage, errors, refusal, timeout, and retry behavior
Model output consumed by code must pass strict schema validation
Agent context is assembled from authorized inputs and a recorded retrieval manifest
Agent authority is a short-lived per-task capability set narrower than the initiating user
Tools have immutable versions, strict schemas, risk level, scopes, timeout, network policy, and idempotency behavior
Secrets are injected by a credential proxy and never enter prompts or model-visible arguments
Agent loops have maximum model calls, tool calls, tokens, time, cost, and handoffs
Tool calls are validated, authorized, approved when needed, executed, and output-scanned
Runtime code execution is isolated by CPU, memory, filesystem, network, and duration
Every output records model, prompt, agent, tool, context, citation, usage, cost, and reviewer lineage
Evals cover instruction following, schema validity, correctness, retrieval, tool selection, arguments, safety, handoff, latency, and cost
Agent releases require held-out deterministic, adversarial, and human-calibrated eval gates
Production feedback can be curated into versioned eval cases without leaking tenant data
Administrators can disable one agent, tool, model, tenant, or global execution class within 60 seconds
Agent memory scopes are none, execution, user-private, or workspace-shared with explicit ACL, retention, and purpose
Durable memory writes are explicit, typed, versioned, provenance-backed operations and never an implicit side effect of model text
Authorized users can inspect, correct, export, and delete durable memory without rewriting historical run evidence
User, source, permission, retention, and workspace deletion propagates to memory and all memory-derived context
Plans and prices are versioned platform data
Stripe Checkout creates subscriptions using server-selected price mappings
Stripe webhooks authoritatively update customer, subscription, invoice, and payment state
Entitlements enforce features, seats, storage, runs, tasks, model spend, connectors, and retention
Usage reservations prevent concurrent work from overspending a limit
Usage and credits use append-only idempotent ledgers
Billing admins can view current usage, forecast, limits, invoices, plan, and payment status
Trials, upgrades, downgrades, cancellation, grace periods, and payment failure have explicit behavior
Product access degrades safely during billing-provider failure
Every billable event traces to its source run, task, integration, or storage object
Integrations use one provider-neutral lifecycle and health model
OAuth uses server-generated state, PKCE where supported, clean callbacks, least privilege, and encrypted credentials
API-key integrations validate, encrypt, rotate, revoke, and never return raw secrets
Initial and incremental sync use durable cursors and generation fencing
Signed webhooks are verified against raw body, timestamp checked, deduplicated, and replayable
Provider rate limits, pagination, backoff, token expiry, and partial failures are normalized
Outbound writes use stable idempotency keys and reconciliation
Connection removal revokes provider access where possible and follows configured data-deletion policy
Admins can pause, resume, resync, reauthorize, inspect, and remove connections
Supported providers pass recorded contract tests and real sandbox acceptance
Comments support mentions, reactions, editing policy, deletion policy, and attachment references
Users can follow workflows and runs and configure notification preferences
Activity feeds distinguish product activity from immutable audit events
Global search covers workflows, runs, tasks, agents, people, documents, entities, and settings allowed to the user
Command palette provides keyboard-accessible navigation and safe actions
Saved views support filters, columns, sorting, sharing, and ownership
Dashboard cards drill into the exact filtered data behind the metric
Reports cover throughput, cycle time, wait time, failure, automation, agent quality, cost, SLA, and returned time
Report data can be filtered, exported, and scheduled according to permissions
The web application is installable and safely updates without interrupting active work
Offline behavior is explicit, policy-aware, and limited to safe cached data and drafts
Push subscriptions are device-scoped, revocable, payload-minimized, and permission checked at delivery and click
Guests receive expiring, revocable access to one exact resource/action and cannot browse workspace metadata
Guest identity, invitation, session, action, download, and revocation are auditable
All first-party UI strings, formatting, validation, email, help, and exports use the localization system
English, Hindi, Spanish, French, German, and Japanese complete production translation and linguistic QA
Current and previous major Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari plus current iOS Safari and Android Chrome are supported
Every critical journey passes the defined keyboard, zoom/reflow, voice-control, and screen-reader matrix
Users can search versioned help, view current status and changelog, replay onboarding, and submit contextual feedback
Customers can open and follow permissioned support tickets with attachments and service targets
Diagnostic bundles require preview and consent and are redacted, encrypted, expiring, checksummed, and access logged
Product incident banners are authenticated, resilient to status-feed failure, accessible, and dismissible according to severity
Pricing, terms, privacy, DPA, acceptable use, accessibility, subprocessors, and security claims are current and owner approved
Every visible feature or integration is labelled LIVE, BETA, DEMO, PLANNED, unavailable, or degraded according to verified reality
A scoped citation-quality or unsafe-output report preserves relevant provenance without granting support broader content access
The public contact flow validates consent, resists abuse, persists and routes the request, acknowledges honestly, and follows retention/deletion policy
Users have a unified inbox for tasks, approvals, mentions, and exceptions
Human tasks support assignee, watchers, due date, priority, SLA, form schema, rich instructions, comments, and attachments
Users can claim, reassign, delegate, complete, reopen, or request clarification
Task forms validate typed data and preserve drafts
Bulk task actions are permission checked and audited
Approvals bind to an exact payload hash and policy version
Approvers can approve, reject, request revision, delegate, or abstain
Approval policies support any-one, all, quorum, ordered, role, group, and separation-of-duties rules
Expiry, reminders, quiet hours, escalations, and fallback approvers are durable
High-risk or irreversible tool actions require explicit approval unless policy forbids them entirely
Mobile task and approval flows require no canvas interaction
Users can request and exchange a single-use email magic link
Users can sign in with Google OIDC
Enterprise users can sign in through configured SAML or OIDC SSO
Sessions use rotating HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookies and can be individually revoked
A user can view and revoke active sessions
A user can belong to multiple workspaces and switch active workspace
A new user can create a workspace or accept an invitation
Administrators can invite, resend, cancel, suspend, restore, and remove members
Roles include owner, admin, builder, member, approver, billing, auditor, and custom roles
Fine-grained permissions apply to resources and actions, not only pages
Service principals and scoped API credentials support rotation, expiry, and revocation
SCIM provisions, updates, suspends, and deprovisions enterprise users and groups
Domain capture and enforced SSO can be configured safely
Every tenant-owned resource has one immutable workspace owner
The server derives and verifies tenant membership on every protected operation
Users can upload supported files with progress, cancellation, size/type validation, and malware scanning
Raw source, normalized content, versions, and parsed artifacts are preserved according to policy
Parsers support PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, TXT, Markdown, HTML, images with OCR, and common email exports
Every source object preserves provider ID, version, permissions, provenance, and deletion state
Documents are chunked using versioned parsing and chunking policies
Embeddings are versioned and can be re-indexed without losing current serving state
Search combines lexical, semantic, metadata, freshness, authority, and relationship signals
Retrieval applies tenant and source permissions before content reaches a model
Results include citations to exact source version and location
Users can inspect sources, sync status, parsing status, permissions, and use lineage
Entity resolution creates canonical people, teams, projects, customers, products, and custom entities
Relationships preserve type, confidence, temporal validity, and provenance
Source changes and deletion propagate to chunks, embeddings, entities, caches, and citations
Retrieval quality has offline and production-shadow evaluation
99.9% monthly availability for interactive API and workflow control plane
99.5% monthly availability for non-critical connector ingestion
p95 cached metadata reads under 400 ms at reference load
p95 accepted mutations under 750 ms, excluding asynchronous completion
p95 task dispatch within 5 seconds of dependency readiness
p95 SSE event delivery within 2 seconds of durable event commit
No cross-tenant access in automated, adversarial, or manual isolation tests
Transactional-data RPO no greater than 15 minutes
Regional recovery RTO no greater than 4 hours
WCAG 2.2 AA for all supported product and marketing flows
No critical or high exploitable security finding at release
No unbounded agent loop, connector retry, queue growth, or tenant spend path
Tenant execution kill switch takes effect within 60 seconds
All acknowledged mutations survive process and single-AZ failure
At-least-once delivery never automatically repeats an UNCERTAIN non-idempotent external effect; certified idempotent or authoritatively reconcilable operations produce zero logical duplicate
Core mobile flows work at 320 CSS px without horizontal page overflow
Core desktop flows work from 1024 through 2560 CSS px
Initial authenticated shell LCP under 2.5 seconds at p75 on reference mobile profile
Interaction to Next Paint under 200 ms at p75 for ordinary UI actions
Cumulative Layout Shift below 0.1 at p75
Telemetry excludes secrets and configured sensitive customer content
Critical operational alerts reach the on-call path within 5 minutes

Knotline-admin permission revocation is effective on the committing transaction; connected-source ACL revocation disappears from all online serving caches, search, citations, and agent context within 5 minutes; server and browser clients fail closed whenever current ACL proof is older than that bound, including while offline, with disconnected ciphertext governed by Section 6.7 rather than presented as remotely erased
Onboarding adapts to role, use case, team size, and connected systems
Users can start from a pattern, natural-language prompt, or blank workflow
The product includes a guided but real first-run experience
Sample data is isolated, labeled, removable, and never confused with production data
Setup progress survives logout and device changes
Every onboarding step can be skipped and resumed
Empty states teach the next useful action without blocking expert users
Local development starts all required dependencies from documented commands
CI reproduces schema, API, worker, web, and end-to-end tests
Infrastructure is fully represented in Terraform
Staging mirrors production topology at smaller capacity
Deployments are progressive, observable, reversible, and compatible with active runs
Database migrations are backward compatible across the deployment window
Metrics, logs, traces, errors, and audit correlation share stable identifiers
Alerts are tied to service objectives and actionable runbooks
Backups, point-in-time recovery, object versioning, and restore procedures are tested
Regional recovery meets the stated RPO and RTO in an exercise
Capacity, fairness, and spend controls are load-tested
Dependency, container, secret, IaC, SAST, DAST, and SBOM controls run in CI

Platform operators authenticate through an origin- and session-isolated workforce identity plane with phishing-resistant MFA, least-privilege duty scopes, prompt offboarding, periodic access review, controlled break glass, and zero workspace-credential acceptance
Runs can start manually, by schedule, webhook, connector event, API, or parent workflow
A run pins one immutable workflow version, policy snapshot, and input set
Dependency-ready tasks dispatch durably and idempotently
Run states include queued, running, waiting, paused, cancelling, cancelled, succeeded, failed, and timed out
Task states include pending, ready, running, waiting, retry-wait, succeeded, failed, skipped, cancelled, and timed out
Attempts preserve worker, timing, input/output references, usage, trace, and error classification
Retries use explicit per-node policies with jitter, limits, and retryable error classes
A failed run can retry from failure or fork while reusing only validated safe outputs
Pause stops new dispatch while preserving in-flight result reconciliation
Cancellation propagates without silently repeating or losing uncertain external effects
Delays, deadlines, recurring schedules, and human waits survive restarts and deployments
Conditions and mappings evaluate deterministically in a restricted expression engine
Loops have explicit maximum iterations and spend/time budgets
Subworkflows preserve correlation, cancellation, usage, and lineage
Every run exposes a monotonically sequenced append-only event timeline
Live state uses SSE with resume and bounded polling fallback
Operators can reconcile stuck work, uncertain operations, and dead-letter items
Per-tenant fairness and concurrency limits prevent noisy-neighbor starvation
Workflows have metadata, owner, tags, status, draft, and published-version pointers
Builders can create, duplicate, import, export, archive, restore, and delete workflows
Builders can generate a workflow from natural language using schema-valid model output
Builders can create workflows from first-party or workspace templates
Node types include trigger, human, agent, approval, condition, delay, loop, subworkflow, transform, and integration action
Builders can add, move, connect, duplicate, group, split, disable, and remove nodes
Edges support conditions, mappings, labels, success paths, failure paths, and default paths
Node inputs and outputs use versioned JSON Schemas
The studio supports zoom, pan, minimap, fit, auto-layout, alignment, multiselect, undo, redo, and keyboard shortcuts
The studio provides a synchronized accessible outline/table view
Edits use optimistic concurrency and display resolvable conflicts
Drafts autosave and visibly indicate saved, saving, offline, or conflict state
Validation detects cycles where forbidden, unreachable nodes, invalid mappings, missing assignments, unavailable agents/tools, policy violations, and absent terminal paths
Builders can dry-run a draft using fixtures without external side effects
Publishing creates an immutable version with content hash and release note
Version history provides visual and semantic diff
Rollback creates a new draft from a previous immutable version
Reusable subworkflows have typed contracts and pinned or compatible version policies
Templates include variables, setup instructions, preview, category, author, and version
Workflows support folders, tags, favorites, saved filters, ownership transfer, and bulk actions
